latest_final:
The speaker has murdered his romantic partner. To explain the partner's disappearance, he invented a cover story: that the partner was so disappointed in him that they walked out forever — "You've disappointed me so much; I'm never coming back." To make that story believable, he forged a farewell note in the partner's voice, writing the line out again and again on the page to work on imitating the partner's hand.

He is the "you" the line accuses; the "I" who supposedly left is the murdered partner. The repeated sentence appears seven times because it is not seven real messages but the same forged note copied over and over — a column of practice attempts.

Sighing, he looks down at the seven tries and sees the fatal flaw: every copy is unmistakably in his own everyday handwriting. He has failed to disguise it as the partner's. The identical script, repeated seven times, betrays that only one hand — his — produced the "goodbye." Realizing the fake note will be recognized as his work and will tie him to what really happened to the partner, he mutters, "Sigh, I know I'm in trouble." The sigh marks the moment his forgery has failed and his cover story is about to collapse.
